clue.text: Markers following rise of saliva

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: in a down entry a rise reads upwards, so the whole run of letters is turned back to front

parts.note: saliva is spittle

explanation.surface: Someone spotting pens just after watching a person drool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise of' turns SPITTLE plus F, which comes after it, giving the whole thing upside down in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Felt-nibbed pens are used for marking, so they are markers.

clue.text: A person about to remain inactive in the workplace

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: a person is one, as in 'one never knows'
to sit is to stay idle and do nothing

explanation.surface: Someone who is supposed to be working is about to do nothing at the office.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done on-site happens at the place of work itself.

clue.text: Lazy Sunday group who apparently weren't bigheaded

explanation.surface: A sixties band whose name suggests their heads were modest in size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lazy Sunday' was a 1968 hit for the London mod band; the second reading takes the name literally, faces that were small rather than big.
explanation.definitionFit: The band that recorded the song Lazy Sunday; read literally, little visages, the opposite of being swollen-headed.

clue.text: Colossus almost overthrown in congress?

indicators.note: something overthrown is turned upside down, so in this down light the letters run backwards
almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a colossus is a giant, a titan

explanation.surface: A giant statue nearly toppled during a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims TITAN to TITA, and 'overthrown' turns that over. 'Congress' here is sexual congress: a couple at it are having sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at it is a euphemism for having sex, which is what sexual congress means.

clue.text: Basic (unspecified) number of channels

parts.note: N stands for an unspecified number in algebra, which is why the clue adds 'unspecified'
taken as written
rills are small streams or channels

explanation.surface: A plain description of how many channels a TV package offers.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-frills product is stripped down, with nothing extra, so it is basic.

clue.text: Dixie address cursed foul play, excusing leaders

indicators.note: cursed means afflicted or blighted, so the remaining letters are thrown into disorder
excusing means letting off, so the first letter of each word is left out

explanation.surface: Someone from the American South swearing over a dirty trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excusing leaders' drops F and P from FOUL PLAY, leaving OULLAY, which 'cursed' rearranges. Dixie is the American South, where y'all is the plural 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the southern United States the plural form of 'you' used to address a group is this contraction.

clue.text: Excerpt from wise man? Nephews recalled such as Orwell and Eliot

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters taken out run backwards
an excerpt is a passage lifted out of a longer text, here out of the run of clue words

explanation.surface: A quotation from a sage, recited by nephews, about two famous writers.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters SEMANNEP sit across 'wiSE MAN NEPhews'; 'recalled' turns them round. George Orwell and George Eliot were assumed names.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell (Eric Blair) and Eliot (Mary Ann Evans) both wrote under assumed literary names.

clue.text: Press frantically to restrict alien advance, when one's engrossed in this?

definitions.text: Press frantically to restrict alien advance, when one's engrossed in this?

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so one set of letters encloses the other
done frantically means wildly, so these letters are jumbled
engrossed means absorbed into, so one letter is taken into the middle
alien means strange or foreign, so these letters are turned into a strange order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A gamer hammers the buttons to stop the extraterrestrial attack, totally absorbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frantically' and 'alien' are both anagram signals; 'to restrict' and 'engrossed' nest the pieces. The whole clue describes a player of the 1978 arcade game.
explanation.definitionFit: The classic arcade shooting game has players jabbing a button to stop rows of descending extraterrestrials.

clue.text: Charlie rings excessively

parts.note: Charlie is slang for cocaine, and a toot is a snort of it
rings are round, like the letter O, so two of them give two Os

explanation.surface: Someone named Charlie phones far too often.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie is slang for cocaine, and a toot is a sniff of the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Too-too is an old colloquial intensifier meaning overly or extremely.

clue.text: How one chooses a cloth with diagonal ridges

parts.note: twill is a fabric woven with a diagonal ribbed pattern

explanation.surface: A tailor explaining how to pick a ribbed fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting at will means as one pleases, freely making one's own choice.

clue.text: Net behind boat with extra meshing

parts.note: aft is the rear part of a boat

indicators.note: meshing means tangling together, so these letters are woven into a new order

explanation.surface: A fishing net trailed behind a boat with spare mesh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Net' looks like fishing gear but is the definition, money left after deductions; 'meshing' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Net pay is what remains once deductions such as income tax are taken off.

clue.text: Unintended result of withdrawing fuel is shells in Fertile Crescent

indicators.note: withdrawing means drawing back, so these words are read backwards

parts.note: to fuel something is to feed it

indicators.note: the shells of words are their outer letters, the first and last of each

explanation.surface: Pulling out fuel supplies has a knock-on effect in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawing' turns FEED IS into SIDEEF; the first and last letters of Fertile and Crescent add FECT. The Fertile Crescent is the arc of land in the ancient Near East.
explanation.definitionFit: A side effect is a consequence nobody planned, an accidental by-product.

clue.text: Murphy goes round to study wicket and make no progress

indicators.note: goes round means surrounds, so the potato word encloses the others

parts.note: murphy is an Irish slang word for a potato, as is tater
to read a subject is to study it at university
W is the cricket abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A man called Murphy walks round to inspect the cricket pitch and gets nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Murphy and tater are both slang for a potato.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread water is literally to stay afloat in one place, hence figuratively to stand still.

clue.text: Oddly overlooked malleable backing singer's meaningless lyrics

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the letters picked are read in reverse
the odd letters are passed over, so only the even-placed letters are kept

explanation.surface: A pliable backing vocalist sings words with no sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly overlooked' keeps ALAL from malleable, and 'backing' reverses it. 'backing singer' looks like one phrase but splits between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense syllables sung as filler in a song stand in for words with no meaning.

clue.text: Admitted offence less dire when nabbed by retired detective sergeant

indicators.note: nabbed by means caught by, so the jumbled letters sit inside the police letters
retired means withdrawn, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: DS is the police abbreviation for detective sergeant

indicators.note: dire means dreadful, so the letters are put into a dreadful mess

explanation.surface: A crime is judged less serious once a former detective arrests the culprit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dire' is the anagram signal and 'retired' turns the police letters round before they catch the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-confessed wrongdoer owns up to it, by their own avowal.

clue.text: Tag's only working for designation of some airport car parks

definitions.text: designation of some airport car parks

indicators.note: working means being worked over, so the letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A parking label is valid only for a particular airport lot.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of Tag's counts here as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Airports label their cheaper car parks for travellers away many days by how long they stay.

clue.text: Going north, youth tours paradise and old settled project in USA

indicators.note: in a down light going north means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards
tours means goes around, so the youth word encloses the others

parts.note: a lad is a youth
Eden is the biblical paradise garden

explanation.surface: A young traveller heads north, touring heaven and past places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going north' reads the built letters upwards in this down light, after 'tours' has wrapped the youth round the rest. The phrase is American.
explanation.definitionFit: A done deal is an agreement already settled beyond change, an American idiom.

clue.text: Fed Frankenfood-like article

parts.note: Frankenfood is slang for genetically modified food, abbreviated GM
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Something consumed resembling engineered food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed' looks like the past tense of feed; it is an FBI agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A Fed is US slang for an FBI officer, the same figure as a government man.

clue.text: Cut grass on taking over care of animal for the young

indicators.note: on taking means upon taking in, so the grass-cutting word holds the others

parts.note: to mow is to cut grass
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
c/o, written CO, is the postal abbreviation for care of

explanation.surface: A lawn being mown while a creature is looked after.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls, abbreviated O.
explanation.definitionFit: Children's language for a cow, a nursery word for the farm beast.

clue.text: Perhaps flip-flop unit involves transistors, primarily working independently

indicators.note: involves means takes in, so a letter is wrapped inside

parts.note: a flip-flop is one kind of sandal, hence 'perhaps'

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: one is the unit number

explanation.surface: An electronics note on a flip-flop circuit made from transistors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flip-flop' suggests an electronic circuit, given 'transistors', but is footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A standalone device or system functions on its own, without support from anything else.

clue.text: Rely on Privy Council's second for restraining knight

indicators.note: restraining means holding in, so the knight letters are held inside

parts.note: a privy is a toilet, a loo

indicators.note: second means the second letter of the word

explanation.surface: Trusting the Privy Council's deputy to rein in a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' picks the O of Council; 'restraining' holds the knight inside. 'Privy Council' looks like one name but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: To look to someone is to depend on them for help.

clue.text: British, amid ridicule, happen to only partly fill a position

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so one letter sits inside the word for teasing

parts.note: to josh is to tease or make fun of
are, as in 'things are', means exist or take place

explanation.surface: Britons, while being mocked, end up only half-doing a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To job-share is for two people to split one post, each working part of it.

clue.text: Astronomer's first with effect from reflected scattering?

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the word
reflected means mirrored, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: w.e.f. is the abbreviation for with effect from

explanation.surface: An astronomer's earliest observations show light reflected and scattered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scattering' looks like physics, but a scattering is a small number.
explanation.definitionFit: A scattering is a sparse handful, only a small number.

clue.text: Sweeney possibly splitting when in conflict

indicators.note: splitting means breaking apart, so one word is placed in the middle of the other

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'
Sweeney Todd is the demon barber, so Todd is a possible surname for a Sweeney

explanation.surface: A man called Sweeney breaking up a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweeney Todd is the legendary murderous barber of Fleet Street.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at odds is to disagree, to be at variance.

clue.text: Turnaround for Dorothy, worried until now

indicators.note: a turnaround reverses direction, so this short name is read backwards

parts.note: Dot is a short form of Dorothy
ate as in 'what's eating you?', meaning worried

explanation.surface: Dorothy has fretted so far about a change of direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ate' works as 'worried' through the idiom 'what's eating him?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true up to the present is so to date, meaning so far.

clue.text: Laurel's second minute to be arranged with Hardy at last

parts.note: minute, meaning tiny, is wee

indicators.note: at last means the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Laurel's second short film is to be fixed up with Hardy in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurel and Hardy suggests the comedy duo, but laurel is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet bay is the culinary bay tree, the true laurel used for wreaths.
